name: Wilmington
reason: Own flindersandoutback town page names a heritage walking trail and Hancocks Lookout on Horrocks Pass Road; one counted source and a short stop (rule 1 marginal).
objection: A small farming town whose sights are a short heritage trail and a roadside lookout; a visitor passing through gets under an hour.

name: Gladstone
reason: Flindersandoutback town page names the heritage-listed Gladstone Gaol (internment camp, tour) and the Southern Flinders Discovery Centre: a half-hour-plus visit (rule 2).
objection: Small town and a single counted source; the gaol's opening is limited, so it could be only a drive-through.

name: Crystal Brook
reason: Only listed by name among the region's towns; no source names anything to see or do (rule 1/2).
objection: It is a Mid North highway stop where visitors do pass through; a guide might yet name a mural or museum.

name: Spalding
reason: Named only as the southern edge of the region; no source names a thing to see (rule 1/2).
objection: It is the southern gateway and some visitors stop for a bakery or the Broughton River.

name: Wilpena Pound Resort
reason: Accommodation and visitor centre, a business; the place is Wilpena Pound/Ikara-Flinders Ranges NP (rule 2, vehicle/operator not a spot).
objection: The only base in the park and the visitor centre; people do stop here. But it duplicates the Pound as a place.

name: Leigh Creek
reason: Town with its own flindersandoutback page and Wikivoyage coverage as the gateway to the northern Flinders; three counted sources (rule 1, town rule).
objection: A purpose-built mining service town with little to see; the proposer may fold it into another spot.

name: Lyndhurst
reason: Has its own Wikivoyage page with See listings (Talc Alf art works, Ochre Pits, Ochre Cliffs) at the Strzelecki/Oodnadatta junction (rule 1, town rule).
objection: Hamlet of a few dozen; sights are small and one counted source.

name: Copley
reason: Wikivoyage lists a cafe and information stop only; nothing to see or do (rule 2, shop/cafe).
objection: Quandong Cafe is a known roadside stop for travellers.

name: Nepabunna
reason: Community; the only draw is Iga Warta cultural tours, an operator, and visitor access is by arrangement (rule 2, operator).
objection: An Adnyamathanha cultural experience a guide promotes; the operator's place could qualify with a second source.

name: Balcanoona
reason: Park headquarters and shearers quarters accommodation, not a sight (rule 2).
objection: It is the access point for the Gammon Ranges and has a heritage shearers' quarters.

name: Bunyeroo Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au (two counted) name the gorge and its scenic drive to Razorback; a second-tier stop that guides single out (rules 1-3).
objection: It is a gravel drive within a park already likely listed; lookouts on it are folded in here.

name: Arkaroo Rock
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au name the 6,000-year-old Adnyamathanha rock art and its trail (rules 1-2).
objection: A short walk with a small art panel; only an hour at most.

name: Arkaroo Rock Walk
reason: Duplicate of Arkaroo Rock (the walk is how one reaches the art).
objection: The trail is a distinct activity for hikers.

name: Cazneaux Tree
reason: Wikivoyage itself says 'nothing so special about this tree'; a roadside tree is a ten-minute photo stop (rule 3).
objection: A named photographic landmark in the Flinders photographic tradition.

name: Sacred Canyon
reason: Wikivoyage and flindersandoutback (two counted) name the Adnyamathanha engravings in the canyon, with guided tours from the resort (rules 1-2).
objection: Remote 13.5 km gravel road; the site is sacred and visits are restricted to marked areas.

name: Old Wilpena Station
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au name the station precinct with interpretive signs (and Hills Homestead) (rules 1-2).
objection: Little remains of the original buildings; may be only an hour's detour.

name: Rawnsley Bluff
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au name it, but as a bluff/lookout on the Pound's eastern side; Wikivoyage text I opened lists only the Rawnsley Lookout, so a walk to the bluff is a hike rather than a stand-alone stop.
objection: For: a headline eastern view of Wilpena Pound with two counted sources. Against: part of Ikara-Flinders Ranges NP's walks.

name: Rawnsley Lookout
reason: 170 m walk to an information lookout on the Flinders Ranges Way; a short pull-out (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it by name with fossil information.

name: Hucks Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names it: a roadside lookout with carpark and picnic area over ancient sediments; one counted source, a short stop (rule 3 marginal).
objection: For: easy, named by Wikivoyage and on the main road. Against: a short pull-out, 'part of' the Pound walk per the script.

name: Wangara Lookout
reason: Part of the Wilpena Pound hike (7 km walk to a lookout); a feature of the track, not a separate spot (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as its own lookout with a notable view of the Pound.

name: Razorback Lookout
reason: Lookout on the Bunyeroo Gorge drive; kept inside Bunyeroo Gorge (rule 3, part of a larger spot).
objection: Wikivoyage promotes the famous Razorback photo of the track into the Pound.

name: Brachina Lookout
reason: Midway stop on the Brachina Gorge geological trail; part of Brachina Gorge (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage calls it an excellent stop.

name: Wilpena Pound Solar Panel Lookout
reason: A lookout over a solar farm beside the resort; minor and not a draw (rule 3).
objection: A short walk with the Living with Land signage near the resort.

name: Living with Land Walk
reason: 1 km interpretive stroll at the resort; one source, minor and a near-duplicate of the resort precinct (rule 3).
objection: Interprets Adnyamathanha and settler life, which is cultural content.

name: Hills Homestead Walk
reason: Wikivoyage: 6.6 km, two hours return from the resort to preserved pioneering sites; one counted source.
objection: For: a 2-hour heritage walk. Against: overlaps Old Wilpena Station/Hills Homestead and is one walk of many in the park.

name: Wilpena Pound Trail (Inside the Pound)
reason: Duplicate of Wilpena Pound (the trail is inside the feature itself) (rule 3).
objection: A 7.9 km walk is a major activity of the park.

name: Trezona Hike
reason: Wikivoyage: 8 km, four-hour walk through the Heysen Range past Ediacaran Trezona Formation and the Ediacaran Golden Spike; one counted source.
objection: For: only Southern Hemisphere golden spike, a geological draw. Against: a single hike among many, the spike is already a separate Wikivoyage item.

name: Boom and Bust Hike
reason: 2 km easy loop near the visitor centre; minor and one source (rule 3).
objection: Easy and near the resort, so a convenient half-hour walk.

name: Chambers Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage names the petroglyphs as the chief attraction and the gorge as a campground; a second-tier stop (rule 1-2).
objection: Remote 4WD-condition track; one counted source.

name: Aroona Ruins
reason: flindersandoutback names scenic ruins and kayaking on Aroona Dam near Leigh Creek; one counted source.
objection: For: a second-tier heritage and water stop. Against: only a blog mention, and ruins are modest.

name: Akurra Trail
reason: A guided cultural tour (operator), not a place (rule: tour/operator).
objection: Adnyamathanha-guided tours of a notable ecosystem near Leigh Creek.

name: Blinman Pools
reason: flindersandoutback names the hike from Parachilna to the Blinman Pools as an outback oasis; one counted source.
objection: For: a real swimming/walk destination. Against: for experienced hikers only and reached by a long walk with no visitor page.

name: Blinman Heritage Mine
reason: southaustralia.com and the flindersandoutback listing (two counted) name the guided historic copper mine tour (rules 1-2).
objection: A small tour that may be run at set times.

name: Parachilna Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage describes the scenic gorge drive between Blinman and Parachilna with free camping, and flindersandoutback lists it (rule 1); second-tier scenic stop.
objection: Mainly a road through a gorge.

name: Prairie Hotel
reason: Famous Parachilna pub (feral food), with three counted sources; a business but a recognised landmark.
objection: For: an outback icon people stop for. Against: it is a pub/accommodation (rule 2 excludes venues that are only restaurants).

name: Southern Flinders Rail Trail
reason: flindersandoutback names the rail trail for cyclists; one counted source.
objection: For: a recreation trail. Against: no detail on the route and a bare list mention.

name: Heritage Rail Trail (Broken Hill to Port Pirie)
reason: A 395 km touring route through 14 towns, not a place (spot is a place).
objection: A promoted route with its own marketing.

name: Bridal Track
reason: One list mention of a 4WD track with no visitor detail; access is via private stations (rule 1/2).
objection: Named by the regional board as the one track to try.

name: Arkaba Walk
reason: A four-night guided luxury walk run by an operator on a private station (operator, rule 2).
objection: A Great Walk of Australia.

name: Elder Range (Merna Mora)
reason: 4WD track accessible only from a private station; a list mention (rule 2).
objection: Named as a top-rated track.

name: Caernarvon Track
reason: flindersandoutback has a listing page and a signature-experiences mention: a top-rated 4WD track; two counted sources.
objection: For: two counted sources. Against: a track with permitted-area restrictions that most visitors cannot drive.

name: Mount Jacob Back Track
reason: One list mention among 4WD tracks; no detail and access via private land (rule 1/2).
objection: Called a top-rated track.

name: Wadna Aboriginal Culture Tours
reason: An operator, not a place (rule: tour/operator).
objection: Two counted sources name it.

name: Ediacara Conservation Park
reason: Wikivoyage names the Ediacara fossil site (Dickinsonia); the site is accessed through guided tours at Nilpena Station, so open access is arguable; one counted source.
objection: For: a world-class fossil site on a World Heritage tentative list. Against: visits are mostly operator tours.

name: Italowie Gorge
reason: The parks.sa.gov.au Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges page names the Italowie Gorge hike past Mount McKinlay Spring with a campground (rule 1, managing agency).
objection: Remote; one counted source and a long hike.

name: Weetootla Gorge
reason: The parks.sa.gov.au page names the Weetootla Gorge hike and campground (rule 1, managing agency).
objection: Remote 4WD-area hike; one counted source.

name: Lake Frome
reason: parks.sa.gov.au names it as a unique feature of the Gammon Ranges (100 km salt lake); 4WD edge access; one counted source.
objection: For: dramatic salt lake. Against: no developed visitor site and the Plains Block is a traditional hunting ground.

name: Arkaroola Observatories
reason: Two counted sources (flindersandoutback) name the public observatories in an International Dark Sky Sanctuary; Wikivoyage mentions the astronomy tours (rule 1-2).
objection: Visits are by guided night tour at the resort.

name: Arkaroola Ridgetop Tour
reason: A guided 4WD tour, an operator product; the place is Arkaroola/Sillers Lookout (spot is a place).
objection: Wikivoyage calls it world famous.

name: Mawson Plateau
reason: Only reached via the Arkaroola ridgetop tour; a tour destination, no open public access of its own (rule 2).
objection: A distinct geological plateau with its own Wikipedia article.

name: Talc Alf Art Works
reason: Wikivoyage lists the sculptures at Lyndhurst as its first See item; one counted source and a short visit.
objection: For: quirky roadside art that travellers stop for. Against: no description, and may be a private gallery.

name: Ochre Cliffs
reason: Wikivoyage names the cliffs 50 km north of Lyndhurst and their Aboriginal use; one counted source.
objection: For: coloured cliffs and cultural meeting place. Against: remote and little visitor information.

name: Ochre Pits (Lyndhurst)
reason: Wikivoyage names the Ochre Pits 2 km north of Lyndhurst, with Aboriginal significance; one counted source, a short stop.
objection: For: easy access. Against: a short stop, same cultural theme as the Ochre Cliffs, and many visitors miss the turnoff.
